it-password-reset.reveal_note: The fake email's sender domain (meridian-it-helpdesk.com) isn't the company's real domain, and the threat of 'permanent suspension in 24 hours' is designed to make you click before you look closely.
red_flags: Sender domain meridian-it-helpdesk.com is not meridianfreight.com
Threat of permanent suspension in 24 hours
Link goes to a different domain over plain http
it-password-reset.what_you_can_do: Don't click. Go to the IT portal yourself, or contact the Help Desk on a number you trust.

package-delivery.reveal_note: The fake uses a generic courier name, a link to an unrelated .top domain, and manufactures urgency about a 'failed delivery attempt' -- the real courier always references your specific order number and links to its own known domain.
red_flags: Sender domain parcel-status.top is not the courier's
Generic sender name 'Delivery Service' and no order number
A redelivery fee and a 24-hour deadline
Link goes to an unrelated domain over http
package-delivery.what_you_can_do: Track the parcel on the courier's own site, and never pay a fee from an email link.

gift-card-request.reveal_note: The fake comes from a free webmail address instead of a company account, asks for gift cards (a classic irreversible-payment scam), and pressures secrecy -- a real request for a purchase goes through the normal expense process, never gift cards over email.
red_flags: Sent from a free webmail address, not the company's
Asks for gift card codes, which can't be traced or reversed
'Keep this between us' stops you checking
gift-card-request.what_you_can_do: Call or message Dana on a channel you already use. Real purchases go through expenses, never gift cards.

account-suspended.reveal_note: The fake's sender address is a lookalike domain (secure-harborline.com vs the bank's real harborlinebank.com) and links straight to a login page, instead of pointing you to open the app or type the bank's URL yourself.
red_flags: Sender domain secure-harborline.com is not harborlinebank.com
Link goes straight to a login page over http
account-suspended.what_you_can_do: Open your bank's app or type its address yourself. Banks never ask you to verify through an email link.

ms365-signin.reveal_note: The fake comes from micros0ft-support-center.com (a zero for the o), not microsoft.com. It threatens deletion in 24 hours, and its link opens a different site over plain http asking for your password, phone and recovery email.
red_flags: Sender domain micros0ft-support-center.com is not microsoft.com (a zero for the 'o')
Generic 'Dear User' and a spelling mistake ('you're')
Link opens a different site over plain http
The page asks for password, phone number and recovery email
ms365-signin.what_you_can_do: Don't click. Type the Microsoft account address yourself to check, and report the email.

dhl-redelivery.reveal_note: The fake comes from dhI-express-parcel.xyz (a capital I for the l), not dhl.com, asks for a $1.99 'fee' with a 24-hour threat, and its page wants your card details. The real notice asks for no payment and links to dhl.com.
red_flags: Domain dhI-express-parcel.xyz is not dhl.com (capital 'I' for 'l')
Asks you to pay a small fee to release a parcel
Link goes to dhl-parcel-release.xyz over http
The page asks for card number and CVV
dhl-redelivery.what_you_can_do: Never pay a fee from an email link. Track the parcel on the courier's own site.

amazon-order.reveal_note: The real notice comes from amazon.com and sends you to your orders in the app. The fake comes from amaz0n-security.xyz, says your order is locked and wants payment details in 12 hours.
amazon-order.what_you_can_do: Don't click. Open the Amazon app or type amazon.com yourself and check Your Orders.

paypal-limited.subject_label: A PayPal account notice, on your phone
paypal-limited.reveal_note: The real notice comes from paypal.com and tells you to open the app. The fake comes from paypa1-support.top (a 1 for the l), threatens to hold your funds and links to an unknown site.
paypal-limited.what_you_can_do: Tap the sender name to check the address, then open PayPal yourself instead of tapping the link.

netflix-payment.reveal_note: The real email comes from netflix.com and needs no action. The fake comes from netflix-payment-update.xyz, shouts that your payment was declined and threatens to delete your account.
netflix-payment.what_you_can_do: Open the Netflix app or type netflix.com yourself to check your billing. Never use a link in the email.

apple-id-locked.subject_label: An Apple ID alert, on your phone
apple-id-locked.reveal_note: The real alert comes from apple.com and tells you to go to account.apple.com yourself. The fake comes from apple-support-verify.top, says your Apple ID is locked and links to an unknown site.
apple-id-locked.what_you_can_do: On a phone, tap the sender name to see the real address. Go to account.apple.com yourself to check.

grab-prize.reveal_note: The real email is a plain receipt from grab.com with nothing to click. The fake comes from grab-prize-draw.top and says you won a prize you never entered, with a 12-hour deadline.
grab-prize.what_you_can_do: You can't win a draw you didn't enter. Delete it, and check offers in the Grab app only.

fedex-duty.reveal_note: The real notice comes from fedex.com and asks for no money. The fake comes from fedex-sg-parcel.xyz, asks for a small duty fee and threatens to destroy the parcel.
red_flags: A small fee to release it
fedex-duty.what_you_can_do: Never pay a fee from an email link. Track the parcel on fedex.com yourself.

iras-refund.reveal_note: The real notice comes from iras.gov.sg and says IRAS never asks for bank details by email. The fake comes from iras-taxrefund.top and asks for exactly that to release a refund.
iras-refund.what_you_can_do: Only use mytax.iras.gov.sg with Singpass. IRAS never asks for bank details by email.

linkedin-views.subject_label: A LinkedIn notice, on your phone
linkedin-views.reveal_note: The real email comes from linkedin.com and names a real person. The fake comes from linkedln-mail.top (an l and n instead of i and n) and baits you with who viewed your profile.
linkedin-views.what_you_can_do: Open the LinkedIn app yourself to see notifications. Don't sign in from a link in a message.

dropbox-storage.reveal_note: The real email comes from dropbox.com and says nothing will be deleted. The fake comes from dropbox-storage-alert.top and threatens to delete your files in 24 hours.
dropbox-storage.what_you_can_do: Check your storage in the Dropbox app or at dropbox.com. Real warnings don't delete files in 24 hours.

teams-voicemail.subject_label: A Teams message, on your phone
teams-voicemail.reveal_note: The real email comes from microsoft.com and shows a real message from a colleague. The fake comes from teams-voicemail.top and wants you to open an .exe file, which is a program, not a voice message.
teams-voicemail.what_you_can_do: Never open an .exe attachment. Check voicemails in the Teams app itself.

zoom-closed.reveal_note: The real email is a meeting invite from zoom.us with a named organiser. The fake comes from zoom-verification.top and threatens to close your account in 24 hours.
zoom-closed.what_you_can_do: Don't verify anything from a link. Open the Zoom app or zoom.us yourself to check your account.

shopee-refund.subject_label: A Shopee order message, on your phone
shopee-refund.reveal_note: The real email comes from shopee.sg and points you to the app. The fake comes from shopee-refund-sg.xyz and asks for your card details to receive a refund.
shopee-refund.what_you_can_do: A refund never needs your card number. Check My Purchases in the Shopee app.

carousell-offer.reveal_note: The real email comes from carousell.com and tells you to meet in person and pay on collection. The fake comes from carousell-secure-pay.top and wants your bank login to release a payment.
carousell-offer.what_you_can_do: Marketplaces never need your bank login. Check offers inside the Carousell app only.

sms-singpost-fee.reveal_note: The real text comes from the SingPost sender name and sends you to singpost.com. The fake comes from a random mobile number, asks for a fee and links to singpost-fee.top.
sms-singpost-fee.what_you_can_do: Ignore texts from unknown numbers about parcels. Check the parcel at singpost.com or in the SingPost app.

sms-dbs-locked.reveal_note: The real text comes from the DBS sender name, carries no link and tells you to call the bank. The fake comes from a mobile number, says your account is locked and links to dbs-unlock.xyz.
sms-dbs-locked.what_you_can_do: Banks don't text you a link to unlock an account. Call the number on the back of your card.

sms-grab-prize.reveal_note: The real text is a plain trip update from the Grab sender name. The fake comes from a mobile number, says you won a prize and links to grab-win.top.
sms-grab-prize.what_you_can_do: You can't win a draw you didn't enter. Delete it, and check offers in the Grab app only.

qr-parking-sticker.subject_label: A QR code at a car park
qr-parking-sticker.reveal_note: The real sign points to the Parking.sg app. The fake is a sticker, shouts PAY NOW, threatens a fine and prints park-sg-pay.top. A QR code never tells you where it leads.
red_flags: A sticker over the real sign
qr-parking-sticker.what_you_can_do: Never pay a fine from a QR sticker. Use the official Parking.sg app, and report the sticker.

qr-hawker-menu.subject_label: A QR code on a hawker table
qr-hawker-menu.reveal_note: The real code opens a menu and you pay when you collect. The fake is a sticker offering 50% off, wants your card number and rushes you with a 10-minute timer.
qr-hawker-menu.what_you_can_do: A menu never needs your card. Ask the stall holder if a code looks stuck on.

qr-missed-parcel.reveal_note: The real card names SingPost and sends you to the SingPost app or a POPStation. The fake says only 'Courier', asks for a fee, sets a 24-hour deadline and prints sp-redeliver.top.
red_flags: A fee to get your parcel
qr-missed-parcel.what_you_can_do: Track the parcel in the courier's own app. Never pay a fee from a card pushed through your door.

singtel-hr-leave.subject_label: A Singtel HR email, on your phone
singtel-hr-leave.reveal_note: The real email comes from singtel.com, uses your name and tells you to open the HR portal from your own bookmark. The fake comes from singtel-hr-portal.top, threatens to cancel your leave and asks for your staff ID and password.
singtel-hr-leave.what_you_can_do: Tap the sender name to check the address. HR never asks for your password; open the HR portal from your own bookmark.

singtel-it-laptop.subject_label: A Singtel IT Service Desk email
singtel-it-laptop.reveal_note: The real email comes from singtel.com, uses your name and needs no action. The fake comes from singtel-it-help.top, threatens to lock your account today and asks for your staff ID and password.
singtel-it-laptop.what_you_can_do: IT never asks for your password by email. Contact the IT Service Desk on a number you already hold.
